claims.statement: spike_w1/common.py is the sole analytics_db connection implementation. Its connect() re-resolves _dsn() on every call (so DSS_DB_* overrides take effect at runtime, not frozen at module import), sets conn.autocommit=True, and issues SET TIME ZONE 'Asia/Shanghai'; spike_w3/common.py re-exports connect/ENTRY_STATIONS/EXIT_STATIONS via an importlib alias (w1_common, registered in sys.modules) so W3 never opens a second connection or copies DSN values.

_dsn() resolves the DSS_DB_HOST / DSS_DB_PORT / DSS_DB_NAME / DSS_DB_USER / DSS_DB_PASSWORD environment overrides against defaults pointing at the local development analytics_db (127.0.0.1:5432); python-dotenv loads the root .env (a missing file is not an error), .env is not committed and .env.example carries the template with the DSS_DB_* block commented out; per project policy the connection credentials never leave the local machine and are never recorded in the repo or wiki.

Every time/shift query must run under SET TIME ZONE 'Asia/Shanghai' because the Postgres session default is UTC while factory time is UTC+8; omitting it displaces every time/shift boundary by 8 hours. connect() applies the session timezone per connection, and the R7 discipline (naive datetime -> TypeError) keeps the Python side consistently aware (Asia/Shanghai).

ods.carbody_history columns are stored uppercase and must be double-quoted as identifiers in SQL ("DATE_EVT", "BODY_ID", "BODY_TYPE", "RW_STATION_ID", "MDS_DATA", "SKID_ID", "SKID_IS_EMPTY"); unquoted lowercase references fail with UndefinedColumn, while string literals use single quotes.
In this environment psycopg2 cursor.execute() returns None, so chained fetch (cur.execute(sql).fetchall()) is a runtime error; every DSS query executes first and then fetches from the cursor.
Full-table window functions are forbidden in DSS SQL because one crashed Postgres; DSS aggregation uses ts-range-bounded GROUP BY instead (e.g. the replay acceptance gate's GT SQL check).

READ-ONLY RED LINE: the DSS performs zero writes to the ods / dim / fct / mart / meta layers (no modification of any table or view in these five layers); DSS artifacts write only to the dss schema, and inside dss DROP + CREATE is permitted.

The complete DSS write surface is confined to the dss schema: dss.work_alert_log (lazily created via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in ensure_work_alert_log, sole writer record_dead_audit with type='dead_car'), dss.dim_weekly_plan (+ companion tables) via plan_loader.ensure_weekly_plan_tables DDL-first then persist_plan (a persistence failure keeps the old data and is reported, not fatal), and the learner DROP+CREATE of dss.dim_* / v2_* / dim_expected_delay. The boot sequence validates the written dss tables by reading information_schema.tables against the DSS_DIM_TABLES list.

The cross-layer read-only reference surface the DSS reads is exactly five SELECT-only external tables: ods.carbody_history (pass-through event stream; incremental consume, per-car late replay, bootstrap replay, and freshness signals S2/S3), dim.dim_vehicle_profile (external in-process reference set), meta.sync_job_log (ETL job check-in, signal S1), meta.refresh_watermark (ETL-layer watermark, signal S2), and ods.rb_position_data (independent 5-minute snapshot, signal S4).

dim.dim_vehicle_profile serves as the external in-process reference set for the bootstrap cross-check: the reference set is rows with carbody_last_seen_at within [now-hours, now] AND carbody_last_rw_station not in (the 4 exit stations union 5 post-exit stations); cross_check returns (symmetric-difference size, diff% = diff/max(pool, ref)) and a diff% > 1% is a boot warning that is reported, not auto-fixed.

F8 watermark separation: meta.refresh_watermark.ods.carbody_history.max_id is an ETL-layer watermark used only as the B3 S2 diagnostic input and explicitly NOT the DSS starting watermark; the DSS keeps no local state file, so the DSS incremental watermark is the max row ID inside the bootstrap window (BootstrapReport.watermark), kept in process memory, advanced monotonically (set_watermark only raises, never lowers), and a watermark of 0 (empty replay window) aborts startup so the incremental stream never starts from 0.

The incremental consume query is bounded on both sides: WHERE "ID" > :wm AND "DATE_EVT" <= :now ORDER BY "ID". The :now upper bound is mandatory (round-1 review B1): in replay_cursor mode rows with ts > now are skipped until the cursor reaches them (the watermark must not leap over the cursor), and in wall_clock mode data is always in the past so the condition is a no-op; omitting it would make the first replay round pull the whole ~6.3M-row table and exhaust the watermark. Fetched rows are re-sorted by (ts, ID) before dispatch because roughly 52% of real rows are ID/ts out of order.

FreshnessGuard.diagnose probes four read-only ETL signals: S1 = latest meta.sync_job_log row for job_name='refresh_carbody_ods' (fresh when status='success' AND started_at lag < lag_min, default 15); S2 = the meta.refresh_watermark value for source 'ods.carbody_history.max_id' vs MAX("ID") on ods.carbody_history (fresh when gap == 0); S3 = MAX("DATE_EVT") on ods.carbody_history (event_fresh when lag < stale_min, default 30); S4 = MAX(vehicle_updated_at) on ods.rb_position_data (fresh when lag < lag_min). etl_healthy = S1 AND S2 AND S4.

FreshnessGuard.diagnose verdict semantics: if S3 is event_fresh the verdict is '新鲜' (fresh) and the ETL signals are recorded for diagnosis only, never overriding the event-layer fact; if events have stopped and etl_healthy is false the verdict is '断流' (stream cut) and the B3 STALE freeze applies; if events have stopped but etl_healthy is true the verdict is '移交模式A' (genuine line stop) and detection/handling is handed to the B7 station-level white-list logic.

FreshnessGuard.diagnose is strictly read-only (all five queries are SELECT) and is invoked per 5-minute frame by the dashboard in wall mode, where the diagnose dict is the banner payload; it must not be called in replay mode because time penetration makes the verdict meaningless (snapshot invariant F-MED-05).

Rest-day downgrade (expected_silence): the STALE state and the freeze are unchanged, but the label degrades to '无数据属预期' (no data is expected) and is_anomaly becomes False (not counted as an anomaly or into acceptance), while alerts remain frozen.

The B3 STALE freeze scope is alert evaluation plus the dead-vehicle sweep; it does NOT freeze pool consumption or prediction computation, so data backfill after a line-stop recovery stays ordered. check() is the single per-round call point in the main loop.

d0_check.py is the preflight probe for the intranet deployment machine: it measures ETL liveness as MAX("DATE_EVT") on ods.carbody_history (under SET TIME ZONE 'Asia/Shanghai') versus the local UTC+8 clock (lag < 5 min = normal; lag > 30 min = do not start the run, escalate to the intranet data owner) and lists all tables in the dss schema via information_schema.tables.

ods.rb_position_data is a real-time PLC position snapshot refreshed in full every 5 minutes (TRUNCATE+INSERT, so no position history is retained); the DSS uses only its MAX(vehicle_updated_at) as the independent freshness signal S4.
